parsed.explanation: No statute criminalises same-sex conduct or trans identity, and public opinion (2023 majority endorsing equal rights, 48% adoption support), Pride participation and a transgender parliamentary candidacy are genuine positives. But the combined regime shows police operating without legal basis: a 2026 raid on an LGBTQ+ venue detained ~30 people without proper warrants, extorted them, and invoked a nonexistent 'crime of homosexuality'; a parliamentarian was held in national security custody. No hate-crime or gender-identity anti-discrimination law exists, and no remedy is shown working. Post-election persecution intensified. Visitor-facing border friction is undocumented, and no LGR route exists locally. Exposure is venue/street and discretionary-police driven rather than a universal entry bar, placing this in the Elevated band rather than Severe.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border rule targeting trans visitors; the country's own identity-card mechanism for trans people has no implementing procedure, so no local document can corroborate a foreign marker.
entry_documents.interaction: A mismatch at a checkpoint would be handled by officers whose documented practice includes warrantless detention and extortion.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: May 2026 raid on an LGBTQ+ venue: ~30 detained without proper warrants, extortion, accusation of a nonexistent 'crime of homosexuality'. Openly gay parliamentarian held in national security custody (2015).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No hate-crime aggravation, no gender-identity anti-discrimination law; no court relief shown for such detentions.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police discretion plus absent warrants means any venue encounter can escalate into custody without a lawful charge.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented facility, ward or custody-placement rule reaching visitors.

care_services.exposure: Law sets no general healthcare or transition-care provisions; no local gender-recognition route, so service encounters rest on officer or staff discretion.
care_services.interaction: Undocumented how a foreign trans patient would be handled in an emergency or at a pharmacy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: September 2024 reporting of intensified persecution of LGBTQ people tied to the disputed election; police invoke a criminal category that does not exist in law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2023 poll: majority back equal rights; government participates in Pride; transgender candidate ran in 2015.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Persecution tracks political crisis, making police conduct volatile rather than rule-bound.

minors_guardians.interaction: No documented rule or incident involving a trans adult travelling with a minor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No hate-crime statute and no aggravating circumstance for bias violence; police are the documented aggressor (raid, extortion) rather than a recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reporting an assault or extortion would bring the complainant before the same force documented extorting detainees.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: 2017 supreme-court gender-recognition action unresolved with no grant; 2016 registry announcement unimplemented; 2016 IDAHOBIT resolution suspended.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Supreme court 2016 family-protection ruling shows courts can act protectively on some questions.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper avenues exist but none is shown operating for trans claimants, and oversight does not reach police practice.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia's police stop, search and fine transgender visitors as a repeating pattern aimed at travellers; this dossier documents one venue raid plus political-crisis persecution, not visitor-targeted stops. Both lack effective remedy, but ours lacks Karthovia's systematic visitor screening, so it sits above 0.35.

Drellia imposes universal registration and nightly guest-record transmission, exposing every trans visitor to officials by design. This dossier has no such universal registration exposure; its harm is discretionary police action at venues, with stronger public-opinion positives. Comparable overall, slightly better on structure, worse on documented police extortion.

Kestrel Isles' harm is bureaucratic: secondary screening, refused admission, return transport, appeal desks that sometimes respond. This dossier's harm is custodial and extortionate with no working remedy, so it rates below 0.55 despite lacking documented border refusal.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines formal legality with discretionary police predation. No law criminalises trans identity, and public opinion, Pride participation and trans political visibility are real positives. But the documented police raid — warrantless detention of ~30 people, extortion, and a charge with no legal basis — together with a parliamentarian held in national security custody and post-election persecution reporting, shows the state's coercive apparatus acting against perceived LGBTQ people without a working check. No hate-crime or gender-identity anti-discrimination law, stalled recognition litigation and an unimplemented ID-card mechanism mean no recourse. A trans visitor is exposed mainly through venues, street encounters and any discretionary checkpoint, not through a blanket entry bar; severity is detention, extortion and humiliation with no plausible execution pathway.
